 INTERVENOR, DONNA BAKER’S RESPONSE TO ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY
   COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION’S
    OBJECTIONS TO, AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR TESTIMONY

       COMES NOW, Intervenor, Donna Baker (“Baker”), and timely files this Response to

Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s

Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony, filed May 18, 2026, Interchange Item

No. 4726, and in support thereof respectfully shows:

                                        INTRODUCTION

       1.      For the reasons stated herein, Baker respectfully requests that the Administrative

Law Judges overrule each of Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission

Services Corporation’s (“Applicants”) objections to Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and

18 and deny Applicants request to strike Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18.

Applicants’ Objections to, and Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony (“Motion”) fails to properly

object to Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18. Further, Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14,

15, 16, 17, and 18 each fall within an exception to the rule against hearsay and do not constitute

“impermissible expert testimony.” Finally, Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 are each

 admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

                                ARGUMENTS AND AUTHORITIES

A.      Applicants have failed to specifically object to Baker’s exhibits.

        2.       “Evidentiary objections must be timely, specific, and afford the trial court an

opportunity to cure the alleged error, if any.” 1 “The Texas Rules of Evidence require the ALJs to

rule on the specific admissibility of individual testimony and exhibits as they are offered, not in

sweeping classifications.” 2

        3.       Applicants fail to specifically object to any of Baker’s exhibits. 3 Instead, Applicants

make generalized, global objections regarding hearsay, relevance, and non-expert opinions in the

body of the Motion. 4 Applicants’ generalized, global objections are meant to apply to all cited

testimony and exhibits listed in Exhibit A to their Motion. 5 Applicants provide only a list of

Baker’s exhibits to which they object, with “[Hearsay; Non-Expert Opinion]” appearing after the

list of exhibits. 6 Applicants do not specify which objection applies to which exhibit. 7 Applicants

do not show how their generalized arguments regarding hearsay apply to any of Baker’s exhibits. 8

Applicants do not show how any of Baker’s exhibits constitute opinions provided by a non-expert. 9

        4.       Applicants’ generalized, global objections to Baker’s exhibits do not meet the

required standards under the Texas Rules of Evidence. 10 Therefore, all of Applicants’ objections

 to Baker’s exhibits must be overruled. 11

B.      Even if Applicants had properly objected to Baker’s exhibits, each of Baker’s exhibits are
        admissible.

        5.      Without waiving the above argument, should the Administrative Law Judges find

that Applicants’ objections meet the specificity requirements under the Texas Rules of Evidence,

Baker will show that each of Applicants’ objections are without merit and must be overruled.

        6.      In their Motion, Applicants object to the following exhibits attached to Baker’s

testimony:

        •    Exhibit 9 – Letter from LUAS regarding archeological sites on tracts 4650, 4651, 4653,
             4655;
        •    Exhibit 12 – Baker Site Archeological Abstract 1;
        •    Exhibit 13 – Analysis of Aboriginal Ceramic Vessel Sherds from Baker Site;
        •    Exhibit 14 – Abstract of Archeological Plant Remains from Baker Site;
        •    Exhibit 15 – Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty Historical Monument;
        •    Exhibit 16 – Photograph of the Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty;
        •    Exhibit 17 – Historical Monument affixed to Sloan Sisters’ Homestead; and
        •    Exhibit 18 – Sloan Spring Flow Study by Texas Water Development Board. 12

Each of these exhibits fall within an exception to the rule against hearsay. Further, none of these

exhibits constitute “impermissible expert testimony.”

        i.      Hearsay

        7.      Hearsay is “a statement that: (1) the declarant does not make while testifying at the

current trial or hearing; and (2) a party offers in evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted

in the statement.” 13

        8.      Under the Texas Rules of Evidence, testimony regarding “[a] reputation in a

community—arising before the controversy—concerning boundaries of land in the community or

        page 8.

ak:\4964.002\Filings\2026-05-26 Baker RSP to OBJ and MTS Exhibits
 customs that affect the land, or concerning general historical events important to that community,

state, or nation” is not excluded by the rule against hearsay, regardless of whether the declarant is

available as a witness. 14

        9.       Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, and 14 each address and relate to archeological sites

located on Baker’s property and in the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8.15

Applicants acknowledge these archeological sites in their application. 16 Archeology, by its

definition, 17 speaks directly to important historical events in a community. Baker’s exhibits 9, 12,

13, and 14 each address historical context and reputation of Baker’s property and the area of

Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 18 Therefore, Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, and 14 fall

within the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against

hearsay under Rule 803(20) and are admissible. Applicants’ hearsay objections to Baker’s exhibits

9, 12, 13, and 14 must be overruled.

        10.      Baker’s exhibits 15 and 16 each relate to the Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty,

signed in 1847, in the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 19 First, neither of these

exhibits fall within the definition of hearsay. Baker does not offer these exhibits to prove the truth

of the matter asserted therein. Exhibit 15 is a photograph taken of a monument erected by the State

of Texas to commemorate the Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty. 20 Baker offers exhibit 15

Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty occurred, not to establish the truth of terms or statements

made in the treaty. 22

        11.     Even if exhibits 15 and 16 were within the definition of hearsay, each would fall

under the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against

hearsay under Texas Rule of Evidence 803(20). Exhibits 15 and 16 each relate to the

Meusebach/Comanche Nation Treaty which occurred in 1847 in the area of Applicants’ proposed

links V2, U9, and K8. 23 This is an important historical event, which has been memorialized by the

State of Texas. 24 Because exhibits 15 and 16 fall within the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or

General History exception to the rule against hearsay under Texas Rule of Evidence 803(20) and

are admissible, Applicants’ hearsay objections to Baker’s exhibits 15 and 16 must be overruled.

        12.     Baker’s exhibit 17 is a photograph of a Historical Monument affixed to Sloan

Sisters’ Homestead. 25 First, exhibit 17 does not fall within the definition of hearsay. Baker does

not offer exhibit 17 to prove the truth of the matter asserted within the Historical Monument.

Instead, Baker offers exhibit 17 merely to show that the Sloan Sisters’ Homestead has a Historical

Monument affixed to it. 26

        13.     Even if Baker’s exhibit 17 was within the definition of hearsay, it would fall under

the Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against hearsay

under Texas Rule of Evidence 803(20). As shown in Baker’s exhibit 17, the Sloan Sister’s

Homestead is an important historical landmark, memorialized by the State of Texas, in the area of

 Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 27 Because exhibit 17 falls within the Reputation

Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against hearsay under Texas Rule

of Evidence 803(20) and is admissible, Applicants’ hearsay objections to Baker’s exhibit 17 must

be overruled.

        14.     Because Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 each fall within the

Reputation Concerning Boundaries or General History exception to the rule against hearsay under

Texas Rule of Evidence 803(20) and are admissible, Applicants’ hearsay objections to Baker’s

exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 must be overruled.

        15.     Under the Texas Rules of Evidence, testimony regarding “[a] record or statement

of a public office if: (A) it sets out: (i) the office’s activities; (ii) a matter observed while under a

legal duty to report, but not including, in a criminal case, a matter observed by law-enforcement

personnel; or (iii) in a civil case or against the government in a criminal case, factual findings from

a legally authorized investigation; and (B) the opponent fails to demonstrate that the source of

information or other circumstances indicate a lack of trustworthiness” is not excluded by the rule

against hearsay, regardless of whether the declarant is available as a witness. 28

        16.     Baker’s exhibit 18 is water flow study performed by the Texas Water Development

Board (“TWDB”), an agency of the State of Texas. 29 One of the TWDB’s main responsibilities is

“collecting and disseminating water-related data.” 30 This report is the factual finding of the TWDB

from a legally authorized investigation i.e., collection and dissemination of water-related data. 31

Therefore it falls within the third category of Texas Rule of Evidence 803(a). Applicants have

 failed to demonstrate or even allege that Baker’s exhibit 18 indicates a lack of trustworthiness. 32

        17.      Because Baker’s exhibit 18 falls within the Public Records exception to the rule

against hearsay under Texas Rule of Evidence 803(8) and is admissible, Applicants’ hearsay

objections to Baker’s exhibit 18 must be overruled.

        ii.      Non-Expert Opinion

        18.      In their Motion, Applicants make a generalized, global objection that multiple

intervenors’ Direct Testimony and attachments “constitute impermissible expert testimony by an

unqualified witness.” 33 Applicants state “[g]enerally, the witnesses are providing opinions

concerning technical matters such as the potential health effects of electric and magnetic fields,

wildlife biology, ecology, hydrology, property valuation and appraisals, electric engineering,

power flow dynamics, or legal requirements.” 34 Applicants do not specifically state which of

Baker’s exhibits they believe constitute impermissible expert testimony or what expert opinions

Baker is attempting to improperly make. 35 Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 each relate

to archaeology and historical information, 36 neither of which is a category in Applicants’ list of

impermissible opinions. 37 Regardless, Baker does not attempt to provide expert opinions

concerning the matters contained in exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17. Instead, Baker is merely

testifying to Baker’s personal knowledge regarding the existence of archeological and historical

sites located on Baker’s property and in the area of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and K8. 38

        19.      Only Baker’s exhibit 18 relates to a category actually in Applicants’ list,39

 hydrology. 40 However, Baker has not included exhibit 18 as an expert opinion, but a fact of which

Baker has personal knowledge regarding flow rate of Sloan Spring. 41

        20.     Because Baker has not offered any “impermissible expert testimony” though her

exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18, Applicants’ non-expert opinion objections to Baker’s

exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 must be overruled.

C.      Baker’s exhibits are admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

        21.     Under Texas Rule of Evidence 107, “[i]f a party introduces part of an act,

declaration, conversation, writing, or recorded statement, an adverse party may inquire into any

other part on the same subject. An adverse party may also introduce any other act, declaration,

conversation, writing, or recorded statement that is necessary to explain or allow the trier of fact

to fully understand the part offered by the opponent.”

        22.     In their application, under “Cultural Resource Sites within 1,000 Feet of the

Alternative Route Links,” Applicants acknowledged that archeological sites 41SS86, 41SS87,

41SS192, 41SS196, and 41SS199 are within 1,000 feet of Applicants’ proposed links V2, U9, and

K8. 42 These are the same archaeological sites referenced in Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, and 14.43

Under Texas Rule of Evidence 107, because Applicants introduced these archaeological sites, as

cultural resources within 1,000 feet of links V2, U9, and K8, Baker is entitled to introduce writings

and recorded statements that are necessary to explain or allow the trier of fact to fully understand

the part offered by Applicants, i.e. the cultural importance of the archeological sites and their

relevant location to links V2, U9, and K8. Therefore, Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, and 14 are

 admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

        23.     Likewise, in their Application, under “Cultural Resource Sites within 1,000 Feet of

the Alternative Route Links,” Applicants also address Official Texas Historical Markers. 44 Baker’s

exhibits 15, 16, and 17 each relate to Official Texas Historical Markers near Applicants’ proposed

links V2, U9, and K8. 45 Because Applicants introduced Official Texas Historical Markers, as

cultural resources within 1,000 feet of their proposed links, Baker is entitled to introduce writings

and recorded statements that are necessary to explain or allow the trier of fact to fully understand

the part offered by Applicants, i.e. the cultural importance of Official Texas Historical Markers

and their relevant location to Applicants’ proposed links. Therefore, Baker’s exhibits 15, 16, and

17 are admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107.

                                             CONCLUSION

        24.     As shown herein, Applicants’ objections to Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16,

17, and 18 are improper as they lack the specificity required under the Texas Rules of Evidence.

This alone is enough for the Administrative Law Judges to overrule each of Applicants’ objections.

However, even if Applicants had properly objected, Applicants’ objections lack merit, as each of

Baker’s objected-to exhibits fall within an exception to the rule against hearsay and do not

constitute “impermissible expert testimony.” Further, Baker’s exhibits 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, and

17 are each admissible under Texas Rule of Evidence 107. Therefore, each of Applicants’

objections to Baker’s exhibits must be overruled and Applicants’ request to strike Baker’s exhibits

9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 must be denied.
